name: BrainTrain 2025
oneLiner: A set of 38 counting and logic exercises, typeset in Beamer with XeLaTeX, released as a PDF in GitHub Releases.
summary: A single-file LaTeX project: `main.tex` assembles a Beamer presentation from five files in `areas/`, which hold 38 exercises in five categories. Each exercise is a pair of slides generated by two macros from `mybraintrainer.sty`: the first slide carries the question, the category badge, the difficulty stars and the time limit, the second carries nothing but the answer plus an optional one-line hint. One layout decision here is interesting: the page format is set by hand to 1080pt × 1920pt with the `landscape` option, so a 16:9 board rather than Beamer's default frame, which makes a slide read like a card for printing rather than a conference foil. A separate commit `01c9d37` cut the step-by-step solutions and left the result alone, which is a deliberate teaching choice rather than a shortcut. The whole publishing layer is one {{term:tagdeploy|tag}}: pushing `v*` builds the PDF in an action and publishes it to Releases, and `.gitignore` deliberately keeps `*.pdf` out of the repository. The trouble is that there is not a single tag in the repo, and nobody in this tree has ever checked whether the typesetting passes at all.
tests: No tests and no verification of the typesetting whatsoever. The review environment has neither `latexmk` nor `xelatex`, so I have not confirmed that `main.tex` compiles without errors.
ci: One workflow, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, triggered only by a push of a `v*` tag: the `build` job typesets `main.tex` through `xu-cheng/latex-action@v4` with XeLaTeX, renames the result to `BrainTrain.pdf` and uploads the artefact, and the `release` job publishes it through `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`. There is no build on push to `main` and none on pull request, so an ordinary commit is not checked at all.

components.name: mybraintrainer.sty
components.description: The macro layer in 101 lines: the `excounter` counter, `\DifficultyStars` on an `ifcase` over 1–3, the time and category badges drawn in TikZ, and the pair `\ExerciseSlide[badge]{stars}{time}{question}` and `\AnswerSlide[badge]{answer}{hint}`, which numbers the exercises itself and opens a `subsection` for each one. The parameterisation knows no arithmetic and no Polish beyond the words in the frame titles.

components.name: mybraintrainer.cls
components.description: A class inheriting from `beamer`: five category colours given directly as HTML (6BAED6, FD8D3C, 9C27B0, 388E3C, D81B60), matching colours for the section buttons, a footer with a link to the repository, and a replacement of Beamer's navigation symbols with a button back to the table of contents. Apart from one hard-coded URL this is a neutral skeleton for any set of cards.

components.name: Workflow build & release
components.description: The 'tag → PDF in Releases' pattern in two jobs, without committing the artefact to the repository. To move it elsewhere you swap `root_file` and the output file name; both actions are pinned to the major only.

components.name: main.tex
components.description: Ties the whole thing together: sets the geometry through `PassOptionsToPackage` before `documentclass`, typesets the title slide, an introductory slide with four blocks and a clickable table of contents made of five coloured buttons, then pulls in the five files from `areas/`. The number 38 is written into the slide text by hand.

components.name: areas/
components.description: The content proper, in five files: basic arithmetic, order of operations, logic puzzles, sequences and patterns, mixed challenges. Each exercise is exactly one call to `\ExerciseSlide` and one to `\AnswerSlide`, with a subcategory badge. The encoding of Polish characters is not consistent here: files 1 and 2 use no accent command at all and stand on raw UTF-8, files 3-5 use them 32, 12 and 20 times respectively, but each of those also has a few raw characters — 64 accent commands against 37 raw UTF-8 characters in total.

overlaps.reason: The same shape: a LaTeX source with its own preamble and macros, a PDF build in CI, the content as the only product. Only an order of magnitude smaller and with no verification of the typesetting at all.
Also a LaTeX book with its own macros and a `latexmk` pipeline, so the typesetting, encoding and CI conventions are shared and worth settling in one place.
The same learning mechanic — a question/answer pair repeated a few dozen times — only in a different medium, and with no progress path in either case.

product: No buyer, and there is no point pretending otherwise. 38 exercises with no application, no timing beyond a stopwatch in your hand, no progress path and no licensed brand is material for one evening, not a product; to sell anything here you would need several hundred exercises and a variant generator instead of content typed in by hand. The real value is personal (something to print for yourself or for a child) and technical-portfolio: this is the smallest example in the set, readable in a quarter of an hour, of a LaTeX pipeline with an automatic release. The {{term:mit|MIT-0}} licence removes even the attribution requirement, so the author has deliberately given up the only return such a set could yield.
highlights: The 38 exercises, counted by `\ExerciseSlide` calls in `areas/`, match to the last one the number declared on the introductory slide and the number of `\AnswerSlide` calls.
The entire mechanics of the set fits in **101 lines** of `mybraintrainer.sty` and comes down to two macros with an automatic exercise counter.
The answer slides show the result only — commit `01c9d37` deliberately removed the step-by-step solutions so that the route cannot be peeked at.
The coloured table of contents is clickable both ways: five `hyperlink` buttons to `hypertarget`, and the way back replaces Beamer's navigation symbols instead of adding a bar of its own.
The whole distribution channel is one `v*` {{term:tagdeploy|tag}}; `.gitignore` excludes `*.pdf` with a comment saying the artefact goes out through Releases only.
gaps: **The repository name does not agree with itself.** The README and the class footer link to `konradcinkusz/BrainTrain`, while the remote is `konradcinkusz/brain-train`, so both badges (CI and release version) show something untrue or do not render at all.
**Zero tags in the repo**, so the release pipeline has never started from this tree, and the README describes publishing the PDF as a process that works.
CI builds nothing on push to `main` and nothing on pull request, so a broken `.tex` will go in unnoticed and only surface at the first tag.

The preamble is inconsistent with the build: no `fontspec` and no `polyglossia` despite XeLaTeX, but `inputenc utf8` and `fontenc T1`, which are redundant under XeLaTeX. Polish hyphenation is not switched on at all.

**The encoding of Polish characters drifts within `areas/` itself, not only between `main.tex` and the exercises.** Across the five exercise files there are 64 accent commands (`\k{a}`, `\'{o}`, `\l{}`, `\'c`, `\'s`) and 37 raw UTF-8 characters, but the split runs file by file: `1-arytmetyka-podstawy.tex` and `2-kolejnosc-dzialan.tex` have not a single accent command (but 1 and 25 raw characters), while `3-zagadki-logiczne.tex`, `4-ciagi-i-wzorce.tex` and `5-mieszane-wyzwania.tex` have 32, 12 and 20 accent commands and still 5, 2 and 4 raw characters. No file holds to one convention consistently. On top of that, a typo in `areas/3-zagadki-logiczne.tex:31` ('naprawde' instead of 'naprawdę') and an unused `\ChunkedTOC` macro defined in `mybraintrainer.sty:91`.
next: Settle the name: rename the repository to `BrainTrain` or fix the three URLs in the README and the `.cls` footer to `brain-train`. Today the badges lie the moment the page is opened.
Add a job to `ci.yml` that builds `main.tex` on `push` and `pull_request`, so broken typesetting is visible before a tag rather than during a release.
Run the build (locally or from a branch in CI) and only then push `v1.0.0`. Today there is no evidence that the PDF is produced at all.
Sort the preamble out for XeLaTeX: `fontspec` plus `polyglossia` with Polish, out with `inputenc` and `fontenc T1`, and settle the character encoding on raw UTF-8 across every file.

Decide what becomes of the set: either write further sections, or write a generator of arithmetic exercises that produces files into `areas/`. Typing them in by hand will not reach a number that makes sense.
risks: A name collision in three places at once: `BrainTrain` in the README, in the class footer and in the artefact name, against `brain-train` as the actual slug. This breaks the badges and makes the repository harder to find.

The name itself is generic and already taken by existing commercial brain-training applications, and the README refers outright to the *Trening Mózgu* series; with any distribution that is a trademark risk.

The repository is effectively abandoned. The content came in over three non-merge commits, not two: `bf4992b` (7 files, +409), `e6e6cc5` (5 files, +544) and `01c9d37` (6 files, +99/-411), preceded by `a7ea22d` 'Initial commit' (2 files, +23) and closed by a single merge of PR #1 — 5 commits in all, figures from `git log --numstat --no-merges`. Last movement 2026-07-19, zero tags.
Both actions in the workflow (`xu-cheng/latex-action@v4`, `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`) are pinned to the major, so the first run will happen on a version nobody here has seen.
headline: Zero tags, zero builds on main — the PDF release has never run
